vocab.title: Match each term to its meaning
defs: the fixed system that puts out a fire in a closed space
a section of the hull that can be closed so water cannot enter
the sound or light that tells everybody on board to react
the order to leave the ship at once, given only by the master
a person killed or injured, or the accident itself in formal use
the recovery of a damaged ship or her cargo
the emergency radio message a ship sends when she needs help
the act of moving everybody out of a ship or a space in an organised way
a personal flotation device for each person on board
an inflatable survival boat that opens in the water

paras: This instruction applies to every ship in the fleet from next month. By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, the crew will have completed the safety round. They will have checked the muster list, the life jackets and the life rafts by name, not only by signature. The deck team will be standing by at the bow and the stern thirty minutes before the pilot arrives.

Why this instruction? In February, a fire started in a machinery space. The fixed fire suppression system put it out in four minutes. The watertight compartment was closed, and nobody sent a distress call. There were no casualties.

But the debrief found problems. Two of the twenty-one people on board went to the wrong muster station, because the list was out of date. Four life jackets were in a locker that was painted shut. Luckily, the order to abandon ship was never given.
By the end of the quarter, the company will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet. Paper alone does not make a ship safe. Practice does.

gist.prompt: Why did the company write this instruction?
choices: Because the fixed fire suppression system did not work.
Because the fire ended well, but the debrief found that the crew were not prepared.
Because several people died in the evacuation.

The text says two people went to the wrong station 'because the list was out of date'.

The company plans to replace the emergency signal cards within three months.
The text says 'By the end of the quarter, the company will have replaced every emergency signal card'. A quarter is three months.

listenings.text: First, I want to say this: the fixed system worked perfectly. Four minutes from detection to control. The compartment was closed, there was no distress call, and nobody was hurt. On paper, it was a good day. But the numbers do not show everything. Two people came to the wrong muster station and asked me where to go. Later, I tried to open the forward locker, and I could not. Somebody had painted it shut at the last dry dock. We were four minutes and a closed door away from a very different day. The order to abandon ship was never given. That is the only reason those two problems did not cost us more.
